newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise gasoline price soon - Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise gasoline price soon - Petkoff.

text.p: Venezuela's Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff confirmed Monday the government's intention to raise domestic gasoline prices by about 30 percent in the next few days.
"I think there will be an increase in the next few days," Petkoff told reporters after making a presentation at a two-day conference organized by British publication The Economist.
Petkoff said the increase would be less than 30 percent.
Local newspapers reported over the weekend that the government would raise gasoline prices an average of 27 percent to bring the average price to 70 bolivars ($0.14) per liter.
The free on board (FOB) price of Venezuelan premium unleaded gasoline Monday was about 15.5 cents per liter.
Under a stand-by loan agreement signed with the International Monetary Fund last July the government hiked gasoline prices 500 percent and pledged to increase them toward market levels.
Petkoff added that subsidies for public transport would be gradually reduced. He gave no timetable.
Gasoline prices have been a sensitive issue in Venezuela since hundreds died in 1989 riots following a price hike.
